---
title: 'Day 8: Repair an electron-pair movement'
---

A **5–10 minute exploration**, using a prediction before each control change. The diagram and result update locally; no network service is used.

## Predict first

Before choosing arrows, identify the electron source and the electron-poor destination in a supplied proton transfer. Can a full-headed electron-pair arrow begin at an isolated H⁺?

## Explore

1. Repair the hydroxide/ethanoic-acid step. Choose both pair movements, set the total product charge and check. Follow the original acid O–H pair rather than treating an arrow as the proton’s path.

2. Select carbonyl addition. Compare moving the π pair to O with keeping C=O unchanged as OH⁻ makes a new bond. Check the carbon bond-order count.

3. Select amine protonation. Count N bonds before and after, then explain where hydronium’s original O–H pair goes. Use the valid-step preset only after making your own attempt.

## Take-away

For one step, state both pair origins, both destinations and the total charge check. Which proposed intermediate would violate ordinary carbon valence?

## Model and limits

Full-headed curved arrows represent electron pairs. Deliberately invalid proposals are included for repair and labelled as such; they are not proposed stable products. The carbonyl case isolates its initial elementary addition only, without claiming a final isolated hydrate yield. A valid ordinary tetrahedral carbon has four bond orders.
